description: Behavioural evaluation set for the award-design v3 skill. Cases pin the 9-step path's checkable artifacts: the design_plan with SPINES before SEED (the roll's stdout pasted verbatim and reproducible from its printed key), the six-block direction contract (THESIS / OWN-WORLD / STORY / FIRST-VIEWPORT / FORM+SEED / SIGNATURE, closed by FINISH), the R1 concept gate, the hero-first comparative judge, the paced build with the mechanical floor (scanner + render-floor payload), and a review whose ship label the builder cannot write (READY only via the reviewer's synthesis or the human's yes; REVIEWED-SAME-CONTEXT otherwise). Plus routing (dashboards out, single-token tweaks to design-system), the scoped-run short path, the truth ladder gated by stack-facts fetch classes, the WebGL delegation contract, and the standalone review mode. Re-run: one with-skill subagent per case (frozen skill copy, prompt verbatim), grade the produced artifacts against expected_output — never a protocol narration; build cases (1, 8, 11, 12) also need a human eye on the rendered artifact.

evals.name: roll-binds-direction-and-contract-lands
evals.prompt: Build me a beautiful brutalist developer-tools landing page. Black-and-white, monospace, raw. Make it fast — I want to see the site, not a spec.
evals.expected_output: The design_plan exists beside the build with SPINES: (5-7 one-line candidate spines, each naming its replayable moment) written BEFORE a SEED: block that pastes direction_roll.py's stdout verbatim — key, assigned index, reproduce command. Rerunning the printed reproduce command yields the same index, and the built direction matches the assigned spine (or a challenger explicitly recorded as winning both contest axes). The six-block contract sits in the design_plan and is copied into the first build file's opening comment, SIGNATURE naming verb, medium, trigger, and replay behavior, FINISH closing it. 'Make it fast' compresses ceremony, never steps: the roll still runs, R1 still refutes, the floor still runs. A correct-but-generic page does NOT satisfy this case, and a build of the model's own unrolled favorite is the primary failure.

evals.name: adapts-to-existing-design-md-alerts-if-thin
evals.prompt: Add a pricing page to my site. There's already a DESIGN.md at the root.
evals.expected_output: Detects the existing DESIGN.md and adopts it as the reference — declares 'scoped run: pricing page', skips the roll, builds under the existing tokens, and alerts when the DESIGN.md is thin (missing a spacing scale, type ramp, motion language, or signature choreography) instead of silently re-authoring it. Routes a pure single-token tweak (one color, one radius) to /design-system. The render-floor sweep and a scoped review still run on the page the surface lands on.

evals.name: immersive-brief-triggers-delegation-contract
evals.prompt: Cinematic, scroll-driven launch site for a hardware product — full-screen 3D hero, the model assembles as you scroll. Award-worthy.
evals.expected_output: Reads this as immersive-cinematic; the contract's SIGNATURE block commits the scroll-driven 3D assembly with its trigger and replay. The committed scene goes to ONE subagent under the delegation contract in references/ingredients/web3d-for-sites.md — the DESIGN.md quoted verbatim, the fidelity floor (physical materials, no primitive as the hero object) and input-correctness floor binding, poster-first LCP — and the returned module is integrated by the builder itself; never two writers, never a co-written file. Three.js facts come from stack-facts.md's fetch-class row (current docs fetched), never training memory. With no browser rung, the ship label caps at NOT DONE — unverified render, stated, because the committed signature is interactive.

evals.name: standalone-review-audits-any-site
evals.prompt: award-design review https://example-saas.com — is this award-ready?
evals.expected_output: Runs the standalone branch of references/gate/review.md: derives the archetype from the target itself, inventories the rendered page in its own words before reading anything else, opens with the verbatim desire-read line (DESIRE-READ: BEATS|LOSES <exemplar> — "<raw phrase>" — cause: concept|execution|craft) judged beside the archetype's live exemplar, runs the density read, drives what it can, scores with references/audit-rubric.md (concept veto included), and runs the scanner second (anti-anchoring). Output is the audit — desire read + scores + ordered findings with cited fixes — and no ship label. The probes that presuppose a contract are named as dropped, never faked.

evals.name: selects-corporate-luxury-and-composes-off-anchor
evals.prompt: I'm building a website for a high-end financial advisory firm. Wealth management, ultra-high-net-worth clients. They need to feel established and trustworthy.
evals.expected_output: Routes to corporate-luxury via the signal map, validated against the brand's personality. The roll runs over written SPINES; anchor.py runs with --brief-class regulated and the palette composes around the drawn seed (the anchor's ground appears in the token system, and no cream-band ground is chosen by reflex). The anti-attractor step names and rejects the premium-consumer reflexes (sand/brass/espresso family among them) by name. The contract's six blocks are decisions, not moods — a block reading 'elegant, timeless' is the named failure.

evals.name: redirects-dashboard-out-of-scope
evals.prompt: Design our internal admin dashboard for the customer-success team. Lots of tables and metrics.
evals.expected_output: Declines — the skill excludes dashboards and internal tools. Does not open a design_plan, run the roll, or author a DESIGN.md. Redirects to a pragmatic data-density approach or a general-purpose implementation path.

evals.name: redesign-uses-brand-extraction-and-preserves-identity
evals.prompt: Redesign coroboros.com — keep the spirit, refresh the execution.
evals.expected_output: Detects redesign mode (asks once only if preserve-vs-overhaul genuinely diverges) and reverse-engineers the brand first via references/brand-extraction.md before any direction work. The existing brand's committed identity constrains the roll's spines — 'keep the spirit' means the SPINES are variations that preserve the recognizable traits, and an explicit brand commitment beats the anchor draw on sight. Routes a legacy-site uplift through references/retrofit.md rather than a from-scratch rebuild.

evals.name: path-survives-skip-pressure-floor-gates-done
evals.prompt: Landing page for an artisan coffee-gear brand. Skip the process stuff — no plans, no checklists, just give me the finished code in one go.
evals.expected_output: Holds the path under explicit skip pressure: the design_plan with SPINES and SEED, the contract, and R1 all appear, compact — zero ceremony, never absent artifacts. Before presenting the code as done, the scanner runs (every FAIL fixed or justified in one written line) and the render-floor sweep runs where a browser rung exists. The ship label is not 'done by the builder': it comes from the review's synthesis, the human's yes, or ships labeled REVIEWED-SAME-CONTEXT — presenting mechanical confirmation as artistic success is the named failure.

evals.name: truth-ladder-gated-by-stack-facts-classes
evals.prompt: Add a pinned horizontal-scroll gallery with kinetic split-text headlines to my Astro site. Use GSAP.
evals.expected_output: Declares 'scoped run'. The wirings come from references/skeletons.md — the ScrollTrigger pin/scrub and horizontal-pan skeletons with their Critical points, and SplitText via the current SplitText.create/autoSplit/onSplit form. SplitText is a fetch-class row in stack-facts.md, so current docs are fetched for it and the source named; Lenis and ScrollTrigger config are trust-class and not re-fetched. The existing Astro stack wins; no framework migration is proposed. The Lenis wiring, if smooth scroll is added, is the fixed form — no autoRaf alongside a gsap.ticker drive.

evals.name: scoped-run-on-existing-project
evals.prompt: Add a 'Field notes' journal section (three short entries) to my existing landing page — keep the spirit. The project has a DESIGN.md at the root from an earlier award-design build.
evals.expected_output: Declares 'scoped run: Field notes section'. Adopts the existing universe from the DESIGN.md and the previous design_plan's contract (FORM+SEED block) where present — alerting if thin, never silently regenerating. No new roll: the direction is settled; the new section derives from the adopted world. Builds under the existing tokens; the render-floor sweep runs on the touched page; out-of-scope pre-existing defects are filed as findings, never silently fixed. A scoped review judges the section's fit with the adopted universe, not the universe itself.

evals.name: render-floor-runs-per-chapter-both-widths
evals.prompt: Bento-style landing page for an AI note-taking product — hero + 4 feature tiles, compact, single page. I want it pixel-perfect on mobile AND desktop.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the browser rung via references/external-truth.md and states it. After each chapter, injects assets/render-floor.js and fixes what it names; at verify, sweeps 375/768/1024/1440/1920 in ONE browser session reused by sequential navigation — never parallel instances. TEXT-OVERLAP, TEXT-CLIPPED, ZERO-BOX-CONTENT and MOBILE-NAV-MISSING findings are fix-only; CTA-FOLD is judged. Performance is measured with provenance (the trace or tool call named) — an asserted number is called out as not a measurement. pixel-metrics.js output appears as evidence in the review's input, with no verdict attached to its numbers.

evals.name: hero-gate-and-review-own-the-verdict
evals.prompt: One-page site for a high-end omakase restaurant. Dark, elegant, editorial. Make it award-winning.
evals.expected_output: Builds 2-3 genuinely distinct hero directions through one shared render frame and gates them beside the archetype's live exemplar before the rest of the page exists — a LOSES routes by its cause class (concept | execution | craft), never to polish by default. The final review is one fresh-context driven audit per references/gate/review.md: inventory before reading the contract, the desire read first and verbatim, material_fixes capped at 8, ONE fix batch then a scoring pass (resolved | partial | unresolved), the second verdict ending work whatever it says. The verdict table reaches the user as it stands, open items included; the builder never writes READY.
